away.headline: NC State loses 2 players for the season, several are questionable. Who's injured?
away.blurb: Head coach Dave Doeren said Monday that offensive lineman Yousef Mugharbil and tight end Vander Ploog are out for the season. Mugharbil sustained a lower leg injury during the Wolfpack’s 31-28 win over Louisville. He recorded a 64.4 offensive grade, according to Pro Football Focus, which was third on the offensive line. Mugharbil also graded out at 70 in pass blocking. The former transfer walk-on put together his best season of college football, earning a career-high 339 snaps. Ploog, a sophomore transfer from Oregon, played eight snaps against Virginia and one against Richmond. He came to Raleigh with a nagging shoulder injury, Doeren said, and could not get healthy. He will be able to return, but it won’t be until after the conclusion of this season. Ploog was spotted prior to the bye week leaving practice in a sling. Sowells was ruled out prior to the Wake Forest game. Doeren said Sowells will have a repair done and return to activities after his rehab is complete. He reiterated that the team hoped the center would be available this season, but the medical staff did not feel like it would make enough progress in the time frame remaining. Richardson was ruled out after the season opener. He sustained a season-ending bicep injury against Virginia and underwent surgery. N.C. State retakes the field this week following its second bye, but the roster continues to take hits. “Feel terrible for him,” Doeren said on Monday. “He was playing so good, and has been such a great leader on our offensive line, and has been through a lot. For those of you that know his story, it’s pretty significant what he went through at Florida. Good news is he has a year to recover fully and have a great season next year. But, in the moment, it hurts to lose such a good player on the offensive line.” Mugharbil collided with a semi-truck during his freshman year at Florida, days before the Gators’ season opener, ending his rookie season. He did not see game action during his time in Gainesville. Mugharbil transferred to Colorado but left shortly after arriving in Boulder. He returned to North Carolina and walked on with the Wolfpack before earning a scholarship and starting job. Offensive lineman Kamen Smith, wide receiver Jojo Trader, running back Duke Scott and safety Tristan Teasdell are also day-to-day. The latter three were injured against the Cardinals. Scott leads the Wolfpack in rushing yards (358) and was ranked No. 33 in the country prior to the Louisville game. The junior has two 100-yard games, including a 148-yard performance against Appalachian State. Teasdell has 17 tackles this season and played 173 snaps in five appearances. Trader played 161 snaps in five games and recorded 221 receiving yards. Finally, Smith played 361 snaps in five games and has been one of the most consistent players on offense, according to PFF. away.headline: NC State vs. Stanford injury report: Duke Scott among many players out
away.blurb: Yousef Mugharbil joined the out-for-season list after the injury he suffered against Louisville, which is a bummer for a guy who has already been through a lot to get back to a point where he’s making an impact on the field. Jimarion McCrimon isn’t listed at all on the report this week, so that’s a positive development, but Kamen Smith is questionable again. Working with a patchwork line is a little easier against the likes of Stanford than Wake or Louisville, at least. Has NC State’s injury situation improved after a week off? No, not really. In addition to missing at least two starting linemen, State will again be without running back Duke Scott, so that’s unfortunate. Not as unfortunate as the Pack’s dilapidated ground game, but not far off. Stanford’s most notable injured player is linebacker Matt Rose, who was a second-team All-ACC player in 2025 after racking up 106 tackles. He hasn’t played in a game for the Cardinal since the last week of September.

picks.headline: Indiana’s Curt Cignetti gives prediction on Michigan starting QB, talks impressive Wolverines
picks.blurb: Defending national champion Indiana is coming off a 19-15 loss to Ohio State that easily could have gone the other way. Now, the Hoosiers will head north to take on Michigan at The Big House, with the Wolverines coming off a 21-18 victory over Penn State. “Out of the frying pan, into the fire, as we get ready for Michigan,” Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti , the reigning back-to-back AP coach of the year, said at his Monday press conference. “Impressive team, especially on defense.” Michigan made a quarterback change from sophomore Bryce Underwood to freshman Tommy Carr at halftime of the win over the Nittany Lions, and head coach Kyle Whittingham has opted not to name a starter for this weekend’s game. “Really tough opponent this week, Michigan,” Cignetti said. “Made a quarterback change in the second half against Penn State. Gave them a shot in the arm, scored three second-half touchdowns to win the game. “Really impressed with their defense, their quickness, their tenacity, the way they play, play in and play out, the way they run to the ball. This is a top-flight defense. “Offensively, they’re got good running backs. Quarterback came in, played really well. The other quarterback has a cannon and can run, makes a lot of plays with his legs. So they’ll be feeling pretty good about themselves after that victory. “It’ll be a very physical football game again, our eighth game in a row. “Looking forward here, not backward. And this will be a very tough challenge.” Here’s what else Cignetti said about Michigan heading into Saturday’s game: Indiana looking to get its run game going “Teams like Ohio State, Michigan, they don’t get up much rushing yardage. We did have some positive runs. We got into kind of a throw mode — I think we called 46 passes and 26 runs — which is very uncharacteristic of us. “It all starts up front. And we all want more consistent production and explosive plays. We haven’t gotten the explosive plays the last two weeks.” On if he will watch high school film on Tommy Carr “You can see what you need to see in the second half of Penn State, in my opinion, which I watched. “I’d assume it would be him. It could be two quarterbacks on the field at the same time. That would not surprise me. They did that at Utah. And the other guy can make plays. “Schematically, they didn’t change a whole lot in the second half.” On playing multiple physical games in a row with no bye week yet “We try to keep them healthy and fresh the best we can the entire season. At this point in the year, there might be a slight tweak, but not major.”

That's because a tough road test awaits them this coming Saturday. Indiana is heading north to take on the Michigan Wolverines in Week 8, and walking out of The Big House with a win won't be easy. Now 6-1, the Hoosiers enter this matchup ranked as the No. 6 team in the country. On the other side, Michigan is 4-2 and unranked. Kyle Whittingham's first season in Ann Arbor has been full of drama, but that doesn't mean the Wolverines aren't a threat to the Hoosiers. Betting odds have been released for this Week 8 Big Ten battle, and proffessional oddsmakers have Indiana on upset alert. Here is a closer look at the early Indiana vs Michigan betting odds, and one question that looms large over this intriguing matchup. Oddsmakers expect Michigan to put up a fight against Indiana For the sixth time in seven games, the Hoosiers are favored in the eyes of Vegas. Via DraftKings Sportsbook, Indiana is currently favored by seven points over Michigan. It's not necessarily surprising to see, as the Hoosiers have undoubtedly looked like the superior team so far this season. But the one-score line shows that oddsmakers expect Michigan to put up a fight. In total, the Wolverines are holding their opponents to 16.2 points per game and lead the Big Ten by surrendering just 256.5 total yards of offense per game. But the offense has been a whole different story. QB Bryce Underwood hasn't taken the next step in his development, and has struggled all season long. Carr was much more efficient as a passer, as he went 5-for-7 for 47 yards. He was also a threat with his legs, totaling 36 yards and a touchdown on the ground. It's just a small sample size, but there's no denying that the Michigan offense looked a lot better with Carr leading the way. Heading into Week 8, Whittingham is keeping his QB decision close to the vest. He has yet to announce a starter, and it seems likely that he waits as long as possible . It's also possible that both Carr and Underwood see playing time against Hoosiers. Curt Cignetti and company have to be ready for anything. The bigger story coming out of the game is the status of quarterback Julian Sayin, who exited in the fourth quarter with an injury. “You know, I don't have a ton of details but he'll probably be out for several weeks,” Day stated . “So, you know, we'll have to come up with a plan there.” Coming out of the bye, Ohio State travels to face USC in Week 9 in another game the Buckeyes need to win. The Trojans are 6-1 and a top-20 team in the country. From there, Ohio State takes on Oregon in Week 10, another tough matchup. Meanwhile, Ohio State fans have to hold their breath on how long Sayin will be out, and exactly how long several weeks turns out to be. The bye week should bring more clarity and comes at a key time for the Buckeyes. Ohio State led 10-7 at halftime and got a late stop on Indiana's final drive. The Hoosiers nearly took the lead when wide receiver Nick Marsh hauled in a potential game-winning touchdown, but he wasn't able to stay inbounds. The Buckeyes can feel good about winning on the road despite a poor performance. However, there's real reason to worry about the quarterback position. Ryan Day gives update on Julian Sayin Sayin wasn't having his best day before he left the game. He completed 15-of-29 passes for 235 yards with two touchdown passes and two interceptions. Even so, he is an important part of this offense, and there’s a huge dropoff after him. The Buckeyes could be without him for a while. Sayin was seen in the fourth quarter with his right arm in a sling. Following the game, Ohio State head coach Ryan Day gave an update on his starting quarterback. That's bad news for Ohio State with their two-year starter set to miss time. The good news is the Buckeyes have a bye week next week. That extra time will help the cause if Sayin indeed only misses several weeks. Ohio State's schedule doesn't get any easier The Buckeyes close the regular season with Northwestern, Nebraska, and Michigan. There isn't an easy game left on the schedule, and Ohio State is officially in the meat grinder portion of its season. Timing matters here, and losing the starting quarterback right before this stretch is about as rough as it gets. Luke Fahey's first action didn't inspire confidence Ohio State very well may have to lean on true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey against several good teams, and that's going to be tough for the offense. home.blurb: With Michigan desperately needing to get its offense back on track, three additional starting offensive linemen have appeared on the team's injury report , raising serious concerns about who will be available to protect quarterback Bryce Underwood on Saturday. According to the latest player availability report released Wednesday evening , starting center Jake Guarnera and right guard Brady Norton are both questionable for Saturday's matchup. Meanwhile, starting left guard Nathan Efobi is listed as probable after suffering an apparent injury during Michigan's October 3 loss to Minnesota. Making matters worse, starting right tackle Andrew Sprague has already been ruled out for a fourth consecutive game. That means four of Michigan's starting offensive linemen are dealing with injuries heading into a game the Wolverines cannot afford to lose. The report also raises concerns on the defensive side of the football, where starting defensive ends Dom Nichols and John Henry Daley are both questionable. home.headline: Michigan Football Injury Report: Week 7 vs Penn State
home.blurb: We are two hours out from the Michigan Wolverines hosting Penn State, meaning the final injury report of the week has been released. Here are all the injury details you need to know for this week’s contest. First off, it’s great to see both wide receiver Andrew Marsh and left guard Nate Efobi completely off the injury report heading into this game. They were both listed as probable earlier this week, so it was likely they would be good to play in this game. But you never know how injuries develop over the course of a week, so it’s reassuring to see them absent from the final report. Unfortunately, the same cannot be said for a few other offensive lineman. Right tackle Andrew Sprague continues to be out as he deals with an undisclosed ailment. Right guard Brady Norton is also out for this week’s game. Center Jake Guarnera is also a game-time decision, which would be another pretty big blow to the offensive line. Additionally, senior tight end Zack Marshall is set to miss today’s game against the Nittany Lions. Marshall has not been on the injury report all week long, so it’s very interesting that he is now listed as out. Hopefully we learn more about why he wasbn’t able to suit up today during Kyle Whittingham’s postgame press conference. Finally, the defense at least appears to be healthy heading into this game. Also listed as questionable all week long, starting edge rushers Dom Nichols and John Henry Daley, as well as linebacker Aisea Moa, are nowhere to be seen on the injury report. home.blurb: There were six total offensive linemen listed as either OUT, Questionable, or Probable entering Week 7 against the Nittany Lions. Being listed as probable, there should be no concern that Efobi plays this weekend. But seeing both Brady Norton and Jake Guarnera as 'Questionable' signals some concern. The only bright spot in the availability for the offensive line is that Babalola has been listed as 'Questionable' instead of 'OUT'. Edge rushers remain Questionable Both John Henry Daley and Dom Nichols remain 'Questionable' for the third week in a row. Nichols barely played against Minnesota, but Daley continues to play a large role. Hopefully, a week's break gave Nichols enough time to get ready for the Nittany Lions. However, the good thing for Michigan is that the Wolverines' edge rusher depth is really strong. Freshman Tariq Boney has come out of nowhere and has become one of the Wolverines' best pass rushers on the team. Nate Marshall has been steady, and that duo has bumped veteran Cam Brandt down to third string — while mixing inside. picks.headline: Auburn vs LSU early predictions, picks, odds for Week 8
picks.blurb: Auburn is ready to return to its home field after pulling off one of college football's most stunning upsets in Week 7 over then-No. 1 Georgia. Auburn won the turnover battle, 3-0, and ran the football efficiently, outgaining the Bulldogs, 192-113, in what was arguably its cleanest game of the season. LSU bounced back from Week 6's loss at Kentucky by shutting out then-No. 19 Mississippi State in Baton Rouge, 31-0. The Tigers took advantage of a Kamario Taylor-less Mississippi State squad, outgaining them, 379-291. This week marks the second straight week Auburn has had to prepare for a top SEC squad in terms of production. LSU is the SEC-best in total offense (504 yards per game), defense (256.4 yards allowed per game), first downs (28 per game), and passing (308 yards per game). The Bayou Bengals rank in the top five in several other categories, including points per game, points allowed per game, and time of possession. However, Auburn proved in Athens last week that stats do not matter and that being more physical can be enough to win. A key storyline to follow is the battle between two first-year head coaches, Alex Golesh and Lane Kiffin. Kiffin is 2-3 against Auburn as a head coach, and has won his last two games against the Tigers (2022 and 2023 at Ole Miss). Golesh has never faced Kiffin as a head coach. Another storyline is the rivalry renewal between two old-school SEC West teams. Auburn and LSU have not played since the 2023 season, and LSU leads the series, 30-24-1 over Auburn . Live updates: Auburn coach Alex Golesh previews No. 18 LSU in Monday press conference
picks.blurb: It’s victory Monday for Auburn football , coming off its 27-24 victory over No. 1 Georgia. The Tigers now turn the page to No. 18 LSU in their first matchup in four years inside Jordan-Hare Stadium. Auburn coach Alex Golesh, offensive coordinator Joel Gordon and defensive coordinator DJ Durkin takes the podium to rewind Saturday’s upset over the Bulldogs and preview this weekend’s LSU game. Follow along the press conferences below: Golesh starts the presser saying that he was most proud of his team’s response and not flinching during the Georgia game. Golesh says that defensively the three turnovers was the story of the game. Golesh says he focused on the things to clean up, which included penalties on both sides of the ball. Adds that he wants to continue harping on his team’s fundamentals heading into the back half of the season. Golesh says the entire team was in the facility on Sunday to watch film and prepare for LSU. Golesh says they are going to need a huge week of preparation to compete at a high level against LSU. Golesh says they need to continue to create advantages on offense. Golesh says they are still working through things with Xavier Atkins. No status on a return as of yet after missing the Georgia game. Golesh says Auburn’s defense was “drastically” better against Georgia on Saturday. Golesh says they worked through Auburn’s advantages on offense when calling plays during the Georgia game. Adds that execution and effort also played in how effective the offense was last weekend. Golesh says that the sophomores on defense are learning and growing into major roles on the team. Adds that they are forcing them to get better on a week-to-week basis. Golesh says that he doesn’t want the Georgia win to cover up everything else they are still improving across the team. Golesh says fundamentals, technique and process is the mindset he’s preaching to his team heading into the second half of the season. Golesh says that he wants his group to remain humble after the Georgia win, knowing the level of competition in the SEC and teams they still have to face this season. Golesh says the tight ends took a big step last weekend. Adds that Jake Johnson played with some of the most emotions he has all season. Golesh says that he told his team to listen to your inner circle, as in the coaches and teammates to help them stay grounded during an up and down season. Golesh says the shovel pass on fourth down came from Jeremiah Cobb fighting for extra yards and playing with violence on that play. Golesh says that he was disappointed in the uncharacteristic drops from his wide receivers. However, he believes that position group experience as a whole will help in their season progression. Gordon says the wide receiver played all day long and that they took steps on the perimeter blocking. Gordon said it was better execution across the board that helped with the offensive flow throughout the game. Gordon says the offense was more consistent and that they strained more when it came down to moving the ball down the field. Gordon says the plan they had on Georgia was “really good” and believes they got out their own way last weekend and was more consistent on first downs. Gordon says there is still rooms for growth following the Georgia game. Gordon says that they looked at everything possible during the bye week to find consistency in the offense. Adds that he hopes to have as much carryover week-to-week when putting together offensive gameplans. Gordon says quarterback Byrum Brown is “as tough as they come”. Adds that he wanted the balls in his hands against Georgia. Gordon says Brown’s confidence was there early in the Georgia game. Adds that he has stayed true to his process under center. Gordon says the offensive line performance is what it’s going to have to take to win games in the SEC. Gordon says to thrive in this league you can’t be one dimensional as a play caller. Durkin says LSU does a great job with their tempo on offense. Durkin says he thought the linebackers played well without Xavier Atkins. Adds that Elijah Melendez and Bryce Deas led the group in production. Durkin says that Cody Sigler motivates the defense to play better every game with his heart and drive as a player. Durkin says the defense answered the challenge when going against the run at Georgia. Durkin says that Jared Smith has the intangibles to be one of the best players in the country. However, his consistency is the one thing he wants him to grow as a contributor on the defense. Durkin says safety AnQuon Fegans has responded well to difficult coaching. Adds that showed against Georgia and says the sky is the limit for him in the back half of the season. Durkin says him and Golesh spoke during the game when Auburn trailed 14-0 against Geogia. Adds that they both were not worried when climbing out of that hole, and that every game they talk in between drives like that. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit al.com. Harris, who later wore a protective walking boot on Saturday, leads LSU in receiving yards with 456 this season on 27 catches. The junior transfer from Hawaii also is first in touchdown catches with five and in average yards per catch among those who have caught more than three passes at 16.9. “The more passes he throws me and the more plays I make, the more he's going to trust me to make that play on critical downs and when we need plays,” Harris said. “I'm just really happy for him.” Leavitt is coming off of one of his best games as he completed 31 of 38 passes for 289 yards and a season-high four touchdowns. “He's just a gamer,” Harris said. Harris has also noticed that about running back Dilin Jones. “Every time he gets the ball, he's dropping somebody,” Harris said of Jones, who rushed 18 times for 84 yards and caught eight passes for 58 yards with 54 of those coming after contact. “He makes somebody fall every time. He's NOT going down on the first guy. So if you see your teammate playing that hard, it just matters more to him. So it's going to matter more to you. You want to block for him. home.headline: Georgia football’s Gunner Stockton injury update after concussion scare vs. Auburn
home.blurb: Further helping things out is that Georgia is headed for a bye week, as the team certainly looked like it could use some time off as it fell apart down the stretch against Auburn. The Georgia football program is currently scrambling for answers following its puzzling loss at home to the unranked Auburn Tigers on Saturday. Gunner Stockton turned in arguably his worst performance as the team’s starter in this one, throwing multiple interceptions and committing a costly fumble late, just as Georgia was driving to try to win the game. Earlier in the game, Stockton had exited briefly after taking a blow to the head, and now, the team has gotten the latest update on his status moving forward. “Georgia QB Gunner Stockton said to be showing no concussion symptoms after Auburn loss,” reported Marc Weiszer of the Athens Banner-Herald on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Some fans joked in poor taste that Stockton seemed to be showing concussion symptoms during the game itself on Saturday, tossing several wildly inaccurate throws and overall looking like a shell of his usual self against an upset-minded Tigers team. The good news for the Bulldogs was that several teams around them in the rankings also fell on Saturday in upset fashion, meaning that Georgia only dropped to number five in this week’s AP Poll, not that Kirby Smart is likely to be putting too much stock into that at this point in the season. However, they’ll have to regroup in time to face the Florida Gators on Halloween, a team that pulled off an upset of its own on Saturday against the Texas Longhorns. Kickoff for that game is set for 3:30 pm ET. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. picks.headline: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams
picks.blurb: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Thunder stifle Wemby, Spurs World Series preview 76ers beat Knicks War of words over Hurts NFL Power Rankings Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams John Adams, Knoxville News Sentinel Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:06 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Georgia's Kirby Smart has won so much for so long that he's regarded as the best coach in college football . But after a last-second loss to Auburn, he proved he can also be one of the sport's best quotes. "Humility is a week away," he said. Tennessee coach Josh Heupel would be wise to paraphrase Smart's comment before the Vols take on South Carolina at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia. The Vols are coming off a dominant 26-10 victory over Alabama . They're 6-1 and on the cusp of the top 10. But all they gained from a victory over their archrival could be lost with a loss to the unranked Gamecocks. Tennessee 26, South Carolina 16: In an unpredictable SEC season, team performances have varied drastically from one Saturday to the next. Based on that trend, Tennessee could be next in line to take a tumble after a big win. But amid all the SEC's inconsistency, UT's defense has remained steadfast. Something else to consider: Tennessee has been coming on strong in the second half; in South Carolina's last five SEC games dating back to last season, it has lost leads of 27, 16 and 17 points. LSU 31, Auburn 23: While I believe Tennessee's defense will prevent a letdown against South Carolina, I'm not as confident about Auburn's chances for prosperity after upsetting No. 1 Georgia. The LSU offense hasn't always been the model of consistency, but neither has Auburn's. LSU's challenge: Winning on the road. It already has lost at Ole Miss and Kentucky. That's a carryover from the Brian Kelly era. The Tigers lost all four of their SEC road games in 2025. They also lost their last two conference road games in 2024. So, they will take an eight-game SEC road losing streak with them to Jordan-Hare Stadium. They're due. Alabama 30, Texas A&M 15: The Tide also are due for a win after losing back-to-back games against Georgia and Tennessee. They can be grateful that their schedule offers a home game against the three-loss Aggies, who have lost two SEC games by 21 or more points. Texas A&M's 41-0 victory over The Citadel hardly qualifies as the beginning of a turnaround. However, it at least demonstrated that the Aggies aren't devoid of young talent. Freshman running back KJ Edwards led Texas A&M with 116 yards rushing on 16 carries. Freshman wide receiver Aaron Gregory led the Aggies' injury-depleted receiving corps with six catches for 94 yards. Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 20: This matchup is all about quarterbacks. You can't be sure if Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor is healthy enough to play. Without him, Mississippi State lost 31-0 to LSU. With him, it scored 38 points against Minnesota and 41 on South Carolina. The health of Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't an issue. Performance is his problem. Mateer is a fiery competitor and a running threat. But he doesn't protect the football. He has lost two fumbles and thrown seven interceptions in six games. And he has thrown only two more touchdown passes than interceptions. In Mateer's last season at Washington State (2024), he threw seven interceptions in 12 games. He also threw 29 touchdown passes. Texas 30, Ole Miss 27: The Longhorns are getting less for their NIL money than any other program. But just because you have a big-bucks payroll doesn't mean you have a big-play offense. Texas has scored fewer than 24 points in four of its six games. ADAMS: Tennessee football should be well aware of South Carolina threat on road And the Longhorns are on the verge of playing themselves out of the playoffs for a second consecutive season. But they might be catching the Rebels at the right time. A week after beating LSU, Ole Miss lost to Florida by 28 points. Now, it's coming off a 28-point victory over Missouri. Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 23: You might conclude that after five consecutive victories, the Wildcats are about to learn, as Smart said, that "humility is a week away." As accurate as Smart's assessment might be in general, it doesn't apply if you're playing Vanderbilt. Record: 59-14 (.793), 48-26 (.642) against the spread. John Adams is a senior columnist. He may be reached at 865-342-6284 or john.adams@knoxnews.com. Tennessee is facing one of its scariest tests of the season this weekend. After dominating Alabama last weekend in Knoxville, the Vols are set to head to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against South Carolina. It's a classic trap game for Tennessee in a stadium that's been a house of horrors for the program over the last two decades (the Vols are just 2-6 in Columbia since 2008, and one of those wins came in 2020 when fan attendance was limited due to Covid). South Carolina is coming off a bye week after a big road win against Florida earlier this month. ESPN's Greg McElroy picks winner of Tennessee vs South Carolina ESPN's Greg McElroy, who called the Vols' win over Alabama last weekend, thinks Tennessee will falter in Columbia on Saturday. McElroy has South Carolina beating Tennessee 27-24. “Can South Carolina stop the run that keeps Tennessee on schedule?” said McElroy. “Tennessee has 46 runs of 10 or more yards. That's top nine in the country, and Josh Heupel's teams are 71-9 when they run for 150 yards or more. Look, South Carolina is pretty stingy on those runs. So this is strength against strength, and the pick kind of tilts on whether Tennessee's quarterback can hold up his end of the bargain. “I'm going to take South Carolina to win this game 27-24. I think they're going to win on the ground. They're also coming off a bye. Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama. They looked amazing doing it, but we've seen teams elevate and then come back to earth the following week, and I think that could happen for Tennessee right here. Because (Matt) Fuller and (LaNorris) Sellers are going to get yards when that first defender misses. Tennessee's linebackers cannot afford to miss in this game. So that (Fuller and Sellers) will keep the Gamecocks out of third and long — which is where Tennessee's sacks live. It shrinks those pass rushing opportunities that are Tennessee's very best weapon.” “Tennessee's defense is amazing,” added McElroy. “They're sixth in points per drive. They're gonna make this thing super tight. But I just lean towards the Gamecocks in this game and the potential flat spot for the Volunteers — even though they bring the better defense into the matchup. The Gamecocks bring a run game and receivers that can win one-on-one. So we will take the Gamecocks.” Vols fans won't love that pick, but it's hard to blame McElroy, who has been pretty accurate with his predictions this season, based on Tennessee's past history in Columbia. Tennessee is set to take on South Carolina on Saturday in Columbia. The Vols are coming off an emotional win over Alabama. And that win over Alabama combined with Tennessee's poor track record in Williams-Brice Stadium (UT is 2-6 in its last eight games in Columbia) has led to the Vols being put on upset alert this weekend by, well, almost everyone. ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, picked South Carolina to beat Tennessee 27-24 . Former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray, who is also an ESPN analyst, is making a similar prediction. Murray has South Carolina beating Tennessee 24-21. “So it comes down to picking this football game,” said Murray. “I really don't want to do this. I wish I could just not do it, but I've got to. South Carolina 24, Tennessee 21. I'm doing it because I love both teams. And what have we learned this year? Teams coming off an emotional win do not perform well the next week. Tennessee's coming off an emotional win. South Carolina's coming off a bye. The game is in South Carolina. You fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me. We've been doing this all year. It feels like every big time game in college football, the winner loses the next week — especially if it's on the road.” “I love both teams,” added Murray. “… I'm just going with what history has told us this season. Tennessee had an emotional win against Bama. Smoking those cigars all night does not bode well for [recovery] the next day. So they're going on the road. South Carolina's healthy and coming off the bye. South Carolina wins.” I'm sure there will be some analysts here and there who pick Tennessee to win this game, but it seems like the majority of folks are picking South Carolina to come out on top. The Vols are coming off an emotional win over Alabama, but are still road underdogs against an unranked Gamecocks squad. To help preview the matchup in Columbia, I asked questions to Lulu Kesin of The Greenville News to get a better perspective on what South Carolina brings to the table. Here’s what she said. How would you assess this season? How impactful was the win at Florida? “A few months ago nobody thought that Kentucky and Mississippi State would look better in the first half of the season than Texas A&M and Oklahoma, but that’s been the case. South Carolina beat itself in both those losses but the Florida win was the best the defense has looked in SEC play. I think that’s probably the difference maker. The offense has been productive but the defense just couldn’t maintain a lead. “You could tell the success vs Florida, whether that was an interception or a touchdown was contagious and mentally, South Carolina looked the best it had in weeks. “As good as that Florida game was, it’s all about stringing wins together and being consistent in SEC play which starts Saturday vs Tennessee.” How has LaNorris Sellers played this year? What does the offense have around him? “He’s had a lot of great help from both his offensive line and running backs, two things he didn’t have last year. He’s had his fair share of interceptions and bad passes but he also can’t help when his receivers drop the ball, which has led to a few red zone stalls. “He showed flashes of his old self in the Kentucky game and that came out even more against Florida. I think he likes Briles’ system but just wasn’t as consistent as he needed to be in those first few games, especially against Mississippi State and Alabama.” What do you think has led to the defense's success in stopping the run? How have they defended the pass? “The secondary had way too many coverage busts from Mississippi State to Kentucky and even had one against Florida. It’s a night and day difference from the run game defense to passing defense, which I think you can attribute to a lack of communication, execution and just personnel. The defensive front has some veterans and the edge room with or without Dylan Stewart has played really well. I think you started to see the secondary figure things out against Florida, especially with two interceptions.” Are the special teams units still a big advantage under Shane Beamer? “Beamer Ball always comes out here and there but Vicari Swain hasn’t had as much success with his punt returns in SEC play as he has against non-conference teams. “Malik Orsan has been good kicking wise, another area that wasn’t great last year and punter Mason Love is having a solid year too.” How do you see this game playing out? Will the bye week for the Gamecocks be a factor? “Bye weeks are always a factor in my eyes. Two years ago South Carolina was horrible after the first bye. A few weeks later, the Gamecocks beat Oklahoma on the road, had a bye, then went on to beat Texas A&M at home and won five more games. “If this is really like the 2024 season, which also started 3-3, I think South Carolina has to try to catch Tennessee off guard and hope the fans in WillyB can rattle a freshman quarterback. “The Vols do have more momentum coming off the huge win, so pressure is also on them to keep it rolling. away.headline: OU football's fatal flaw haunts Sooners again in collapse vs Kentucky
away.blurb: "We had plenty of opportunities there late into the third quarter to knock them out. We just weren't able to get it done.” With Michael Fasusi, Heath Ozaeta and Eddy Pierre-Louis out due to injury, Fodje was already playing out of position on a line filled with backups. Now, he was in clear pain. “I just listen to the trainers and him, what he’s telling them,” Venables said. “Some guys try to battle through that because they’re able to. He did all he could. If the trainers come over and say somebody’s out or somebody’s up, it goes according to what they say.” “That's just football,” offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle said of the offensive line. “We had opportunities there at the end of the game to go win the football game, and I got to be better in those moments and those situations, putting those guys in a position to be successful, regardless of who's out there. “Whatever 11 we have out there, it is my sole responsibility to put those kids in position to go be successful,” Arbuckle said. “Move the ball down the field, capitalize in those situations, those opportunities, regardless of who was out there. I have to be really good about putting those guys in position to go make the plays, to win the football game. Multiple injuries on the offensive line were a critical factor in the team's late-game collapse. Offensive lineman Ryan Fodje played through an injury, allowing two sacks on a key fourth-quarter drive. Quarterback John Mateer threw three interceptions, including a costly pick-six with just over a minute remaining. NORMAN — Around the midpoint of the third quarter, Ryan Fodje was hurt. Clearly in pain, the second-year Oklahoma offensive lineman limped off the field. Already down three linemen, the training staff re-taped Fodje’s right leg on the sideline and he was back in the game shortly afterward. The Sooners’ offensive line , which held its own for most of Saturday night, unraveled late. Fodje, who struggled to move, allowed two sacks on a critical drive early in the fourth quarter. OU’s offensive line injuries and lack of depth was its fatal flaw in a 21-13 loss to No. 17 Kentucky in which the Sooners outplayed the Wildcats for almost three quarters. With the loss, OU fell to 3-3. The Sooners outgained Kentucky 346-230 but their offense failed to move the ball with any efficiency late due to a decimated offensive line and overall inconsistent decisions. “They made the plays when they needed to, and we weren't able to get it done as a staff or as a team,” said Sooners coach Brent Venables, who is now 58 games into his tenure in which offensive dilemmas are a common theme. OU finally pulled Fodje late, placing Peyton Joseph at left tackle. Venables was asked postgame about the decision to continue playing Fodje even though he was clearly not 100%. away.headline: Oklahoma’s Michael Fasusi comeback might have to wait until after Kentucky showdown
away.blurb: Oklahoma’s starting left tackle appears set to miss another game. After initially being listed as questionable, Fasusi was downgraded to doubtful , joining fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis on the team’s latest injury report. “Oklahoma is again expected to be without starting offensive linemen Michael Fasusi and Eddy Pierre-Louis. Both are doubtful,” Nfl insider Pete Thamel reported. However, Fasusi is not the only Oklahoma offensive lineman dealing with an injury concern ahead of the Kentucky game. Alongside Fasusi and Pierre-Louis, offensive lineman Heath Ozaeta was also listed as doubtful. Meanwhile, Eli Bowen, Jacobe Johnson, Parker Livingstone, Trell Harris, Taylor Heim, Xavier Robinson and Trynae Washington were all listed as out for the upcoming game. Related: Tennessee QB Faizon Brandon available for Alabama clash but there’s a catch Related: Oregon’s Evan Stewart remains doubtful for Nebraska clash Oklahoma football fans were certainly excited by the possibility of Michael Fasusi returning for the showdown against Kentucky, as the offensive tackle has been sidelined since the season opener. However, a new report has now dampened those expectations. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The update is particularly frustrating for Oklahoma fans, as head coach Brent Venables recently offered an encouraging assessment of Fasusi’s recovery during his weekly press conference. His comments suggested that the sophomore was getting closer to returning to the field. Fasusi initially sustained a shoulder injury during training camp but still played against UTEP in the season opener. Unfortunately, he appeared to aggravate the issue during Oklahoma’s opening-game victory, which forced him to miss the following four games. Fasusi’s prolonged absence has been a significant concern for Oklahoma’s offensive line. The sophomore was expected to play an important role this season after establishing himself as a regular starter during his freshman season. Oklahoma is coming off a significant win over Texas and will look to carry that momentum into its matchup against Kentucky. This article originally appeared on Sooners Wire: Pair of former Sooners return as Captains to face Oklahoma The Oklahoma Sooners take on the Kentucky Wildcats on Saturday and will welcome a pair of former Sooners back onto Owen Field. Former wide receiver Nic Anderson and former running back Jovantae Barnes were named captains for the Wildcats ahead of this week's matchup. Both players were key signees for the Sooners in Brent Venables inaugural 2022 recruiting class. Anderson, the younger brother of former running back Rodney Anderson, became a big-time contributor in the 2023 season. He started the year as the No. 4 wide receiver, but moved into the starting lineup when Andrel Anthony was injured. Anderson had a big season, including the game-winning touchdown against the Texas Longhorns in the Red River Showdown. But after an injury-plagued 2024 season, Anderson transferred to LSU, where he played sparingly before joining new head coach Will Stein and the Kentucky Wildcats for 2026. Now both are playing roles for a Kentucky team that's 5-1 and looking to build on their three-game winning streak with a win in a place where they were productive players earlier in their college career. STARKVILLE — Billy Puckett could make a second consecutive start as Mississippi State football's quarterback and face another really good defense. It was the first career start for Puckett, the sophomore from Jackson Prep who walked on to the team last season. He went 16-for-26 with 121 passing yards, no touchdowns, one interception. and 36 rushing yards. "Contrary to what other people believe, I was super comfortable with (Puckett) during the game, and I have all the belief in the world in what he can do," starting center Canon Boone said. away.headline: Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley
away.blurb: The Wildcats are in desperate need of someone to step in for Oakley. He was the leading receiver at the position for K-State a year ago. This season, he is among the top players on the roster with NFL interest. During training camp, Klein said he hosted several NFL scouts who were on campus to check out Oakley. Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Shandel Richardson Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas State Wildcats are expected to once again be without one of their key offensive players this weekend on the road against the Arizona State Sun Devils. K-State coach Collin Klein hinted that tight end Garrett Oakley could miss the third game of the Big 12 conference schedule. Oakley did not play in last week's game against the Kansas Jayhawks in the Sunflower Showdown at Bill Snyder Family Stadium. Here's what Klein had to say during his weekly press conference about the Oakley situation. "Probably unlikely, but we'll see," Klein said. "Day to day." Oakley missed the game because of an undisclosed illness. It gave more opportunities to sophomore Linkon Cure, who is among the most hyped players in program history. He is the first five-star recruit to ever play at Kansas State. While he has gotten off to a slow start, the Wildcats are hoping he can live up to the huge expectations. He has seven catches for 66 yards this season. Last week he caught two passes for 16 yards. The Wildcats need production from Cure because Oakley isn't the only tight end missing. Two weeks ago, it was announced that backup Will Anciaux would miss the season after sustaining a lower leg injury. Klein is also experimenting with moving left tackle Oliver Miller to tight end. That's where he played last week in the win against the Jayhawks. It is unknown if the move is permanent but that's where Miller will play this week. This was a move that was in the works because the Wildcats coaching staff was using him at tight end the past few weeks. A 6-foot-6 freshman, Miller has embraced the opportunity. He was a standout at Cherry Creek (Colo.) High School, where he was rated the No. 41 tackle in the country. Perhaps this could be a better calling for him because of his athleticism. The hope is Oakley is back in uniform sooner than later. He is a big component of the offense and is needed if the Wildcats are going to remain in the hunt for the Big 12 conference championship and College Football Playoff.

away.blurb: Avery Johnson injury updates: Kansas State QB returns after leaving KU game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Story by The Topeka Capital Journal Avery Johnson injury updates: Kansas State QB returns after leaving KU game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads MANHATTAN — Kansas State quarterback Avery Johnson returned to the game after missing one play that resulted in a touchdown. The quarterback was slow to get up after a 59-yard run that set up a four-yard rushing touchdown by Rodney Fields. Backup Jacob Knuth entered the game to hand the ball off to Fields with 13:46 left in the first quarter. Johnson lay on the turf for several minutes before being pulled up by the trainers. He smiled as he got up and had no noticeable limp . At the end of the 59-yard run, he stumbled before falling to the turf. Kansas ' Bryson Hayes returned the ensuing kickoff for a 95-yard touchdown to tie the game at seven with 13:04 left in the opening quarter. On Johnson's first play back, he completed a 45-yard pass to a wide-open Derrick Salley downfield. The Wildcats ran a designed run for Johnson two plays later. away.headline: Kansas State QB Avery Johnson laughs off injury scare in win vs Kansas
away.blurb: After the game, Johnson said he got the wind knocked out of him. He finished the game 14 of 24 for 209 yards and a touchdown through the air, while also rushing for 132 yards. Kansas State QB Avery Johnson laughs off injury scare in win vs Kansas - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Story by The Topeka Capital Journal Kansas State QB Avery Johnson laughs off injury scare in win vs Kansas Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads MANHATTAN — On the fourth play of Kansas State's matchup with Kansas , Wildcats quarterback Avery Johnson found a lane down the middle of the field and took off. Johnson was almost a blur and looked destined for the end zone, but it didn't go that way. An awkward fall to the turf ended his 59-yard run at Kansas ' 4, but no one at Bill Snyder Family Stadium cared that the play didn't result in a touchdown . Johnson lay on the ground for several minutes as trainers attended to him. Never mind the Wildcats' 17-game winning streak over the Jayhawks; it looked like K-State's star quarterback could be seriously hurt. "Y'all know that's my roommate; like, that's my best friend," running back Joe Jackson said. "I almost teared up at least a little bit." picks.headline: ESPN predicts the winner of Clemson football vs. Virginia Tech
picks.blurb: Virginia Tech's Ethan Grunkemeyer leads the Hokies into Memorial Stadium, less than a year after he squared off against the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl at Yankee Stadium while playing for Penn State. In that game, Grunkemeyer threw for 260 yards and two touchdowns in Penn State's 22-10 win over Clemson. A third-year QB who committed to the Nittany Lions and James Franklin, Grunkemeyer followed his former Penn State coach to Blacksburg after Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech last November after the Nittany Lions parted ways with the 12-year skipper barely a month earlier. He has thrown for 1,984 yards and 15 touchdowns to two interceptions through seven games this season. Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech lead the ACC in passing yards , though the Hokies have played one more game than Darian Mensah and the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes. Clemson's passing game has been a complete contrast, to say the least. Through their first six contests, the Tigers have thrown a combined two touchdown psases between Week 1 starter Christopher Vizzina and former four-star freshman Tait Reynolds. The Tigers are second to last in the ACC in total offense with 340.7 yards per game while Virginia Tech ranks sixth (449.7) in the conference. Reynolds was 17 of 26 for 127 yards in Clemson's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern in Week 6. He has thrown for 943 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions entering his fifth start of 2026. Will Clemson football beat Virginia Tech? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Clemson as a 2.5-point favorite over Virginia Tech, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, gives Clemson a 55.9% chance to win. Virginia Tech has a 44.1% chance. The Tigers are No. 48 in ESPN's FPI with a 6.5 rating, which ranks 10th among ACC teams. Virginia Tech has a 6.6 rating that's one spot ahead of Clemson in ESPN's metrics. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Oregon State (6.0) in the FPI. Clemson football has longshot odds of reaching ACC title game entering Week 8 In ESPN's FPI entering Week 8, Clemson's chances of reaching six wins to qualify for a bowl game stand at 88.4%. The Tigers' chances of winning the ACC, however, are just 0.3%. That's down from 0.9% before the Tigers' 41-13 loss to the Miami Hurricanes on Oct. 3. Clemson's chances of reaching the 12-team College Football Playoff are 1.5%, which is down from 4.1% prior to the Miami loss and down from 22.2% entering the season. ACC football teams ranked by ESPN FPI: Who is best suited to beat Miami? There's a big gap between Miami and the rest of the ACC, but here is where Clemson and all 17 conference teams rank in ESPN's FPI: 17. Stanford Cardinal (-11.4 FPI) 16. ESPN explains: "The Football Power Index (FPI) is a measure of team strength that is meant to be the best predictor of a team's performance going forward for the rest of the season. FPI represents how many points above or below average a team is. Projected results are based on 20,000 simulations of the rest of the season using FPI, results to date, and the remaining schedule. Ratings and projections update daily. FPI data from seasons prior to 2019 may not be complete." The final availability report is out for this game, and it includes the final status for running back Justice Haynes, who was listed as doubtful coming into Saturday, as well as offensive lineman Josh Petty and defensive lineman Landen Marshall. RB Justice Haynes and OT Josh Petty are going to be game-time decisions. If Haynes is unable to go today, Trelain Maddox and Chad Alexander would be the top options in the backfield for the Yellow Jackets today against Virginia Tech. Maddox is coming off the best game of his career last week against Duke. Riggs, the Yellow Jackets starting center, came back from an injury last week in the win over Duke, but was hurt during the game and did not return. He was not on the injury report this week and should be starting in the middle of the Yellow Jackets offensive line against what has been one of the ACC's best defensive fronts through the first part of the season. away.headline: Game Preview: Hokies Look To Get Well Against Georgia Tech
away.blurb: His completion percentage drops nearly 25 points, and his yards-per-attempt drops like a rock. When Mendoza is pressured, the Georgia Tech passing game basically ceases to function. That could be Mendoza’s fault, or perhaps the coaching staff just hasn’t figured out how to scheme to beat pressure as of yet. Georgia Tech is still very talented in the backfield, even though McKenzie left to be the running backs coach at Virginia Tech. It has one of the best duos in the ACC. However, one of them (Malachi Hosley) has been limited due to injury and hasn’t played since Week 3. One of the things that stood out to me about Georgia Tech’s season opener vs. Colorado was how badly the Yellow Jackets got beat up front. They were overmatched physically, and it hasn’t been pretty for them this season. Pass blocking: 47.9, No. 17 out of 17. Georgia Tech is a full six points behind Stanford, the second-to-last team. Run blocking: 54.2, No. 15 out of 17. Only Boston College and Syracuse rank lower in run-blocking grade. One number that draws my eye is available yards. Opposing offenses have gained 58.8 percent of the yards available to them against the Yellow Jackets this season, which is one of the highest marks in the country. However, what stands out to me the most is turnovers. The Yellow Jackets haven’t forced a single turnover against an FBS team this year. (Virginia Tech forced three, all against ODU). So, not only do offenses gain well over half of the available yards against Georgia Tech, but the Jackets also haven’t been able to turn them over. That’s a recipe for allowing 29.5 points per game, which ranks No. 97 nationally. We don’t know how many of those players will be available to play against Virginia Tech on Saturday, which is another reason it makes this one more difficult to predict. But since a number of them haven’t played since Week 2, and several others still weren’t able to return to the rotation after the open week, it seems like some of these injuries are long-term problems. Jeffrey Overton’s big return against Pitt aside, Virginia Tech needs to play a lot better on special teams than it has over the last two weeks. That’s not just kicker John Love, but also punter Nathan Totten and the entire operation. Here’s what the Hokies will be facing this week: • Punter Alex Bacchetta : A transfer from Rice, he was a third-team All-AAC performer. He’s averaging 44.2 yards per punt this year, and Georgia Tech has allowed just eight punt return yards on four returns. While the Yellow Jackets also blocked one, they’ve also had one blocked. The Jackets have averaged 14.8 yards per punt return on the season, but they’ve had just four returns. home.blurb: Kelly, a junior, was the Tigers' first transfer that they picked up during the 2026 cycle. Being a three-star transfer recruit coming out of West Georgia, it's not hard to see why Swinney jumped on bringing him to Clemson for at least his next two seasons. Clemson's Defensive Line Receiving 'Shot in the Arm' Returner Against Charleston Southern - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Clemson defensive tackle Kourtney Kelly (44) during the first Spring football practice open to media in Clemson, SC Friday, Feb 27, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Griffin Barfield Wed, October 14, 2026 at 5:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads One of the Clemson Tigers ' duller position groups so far this season has been the interior defensive line. That should change in the near future with a key player coming back from injury. Back at the beginning of the year, the Tigers' defensive tackle transfer Kourtney Kelly tore his ACL, missing the remainder of the spring and the start of the 2026 season. After head coach Dabo Swinney hinted at it over the course of the last several weeks, the expectation is for Kelly to play against Charleston Southern this weekend. Swinney thinks it will give that group a much-needed boost for the remainder of the season. "We kind of ramped him up last week," he said. "He's been getting competitive work, and so that's got a chance to be a good shot in the arm for us down the stretch." Junior lineman Champ Thompson was a guy who worked with Kelly over the first few months that he was still practicing with the team before his injury. Even now, as the West Georgia transfer has worked his way back into practices, he's impressed with the type of work ethic he's had to show to come back in 2026. That will only help the Tigers with adding another piece, but one that is expected to be a starter when fully healthy. "It's awesome," Thompson said. "It was awesome to see him put in the work and be able to try to get back as fast as he could." The Columbus, Georgia, native finished with 17 tackles, four sacks and a fumble recovery in 12 games with the Wolves, redshirting in 2024. Over the course of the first several weeks, when he was healthy, many saw him as the standout transfer from Clemson's 2026 offseason class. Now, in the Tigers' sixth game of the season, fans should see snaps from the defensive tackle against Charleston Southern this weekend. "He's doing really good," Swinney added. "We expect him to play." home.blurb: Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return That progress includes moving from the larger brace to a sleeve and pad. Vizzina is still working to regain his full range of motion, so Swinney's update stops short of confirming a return to game action. True freshman Tait Reynolds took over as Clemson 's starter ahead of the North Carolina game after Vizzina started the first two contests. Vizzina was completely unavailable against the Tar Heels, then dressed against Cal strictly as an emergency option. Swinney made clear just how limited that availability was. Clemson would have turned to Trent Pearman and likely Brock Bradley before asking Vizzina to play against the Golden Bears. This article originally appeared on Clemson Wire: Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return Drew Landon, Clemson Wire Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Christopher Vizzina has not played since suffering a left elbow injury against Georgia Southern in Week 2. His recovery has taken longer than Clemson initially expected, but head coach Dabo Swinney offered an encouraging update following Wednesday's practice. "CV is still not 100%, but this has been the best week he's had since before he got hurt," Swinney said. "He's just gotten better and better. We thought it would bounce back a little bit quicker, but it's just been hard for him," Swinney said. "But he's gotten better. He's had a really good week, and it's just one of those things that's been day-to-day." "It would have been like we would have had to get through Trent and probably even through Brock before we got to him," Swinney said. "He was just still really, really sore." Through his two starts, Vizzina completed 14 of 23 passes for 102 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. home.headline: ACC preseason poll leaves Clemson little margin for error following Zac Foster injury
home.blurb: From a purely optical standpoint, Clemson beating out Florida State by over 100 points to finish in sixth place largely signifies that the Tigers should be an NCAA Tournament team again coming in. The latest Bracketology update from Oct. 6 has Clemson as a No. 11 seed as one of seven ACC teams to make the field, along with Duke, Louisville, Miami, North Carolina, North Carolina State, and Virginia. Of course, this ACC preseason poll was conducted before Zac Foster was ruled out for the season ... Coming into the ACC Tipoff, Clemson head coach Brad Brownell let it be known that Foster and Carter Welling were both working their way back from torn ACLs. Prior to Foster tearing the same one he was rehabbing, he had been on track to return before the end of the calendar year. As for Welling, his return was always coming later on. This is because he tore his ACL down the stretch last March. While Dillon Hunter's eligibility remains in flux, there could be some other good news on the horizon. It should be noted that during the ACC Tipoff, freshman guard Harris Reynolds was one of six players to receive a Preseason ACC Rookie of the Year vote. Although he may be green coming in, there is a real opportunity for him to take advantage of, with Foster out for the year and Hunter currently ineligible. Right now, Clemson has to hold serve during its impressive non-conference schedule to be in a good position to make the NCAA Tournament. There are quality ACC wins to be had, but Clemson cannot afford to start this season out at a deficit in the resume department. Frankly, it could be a baptism by fire right away for the depleted Tigers right out of the gate. Sometimes, you have to fight fire with fire. For the first time in the 90-year history of the AP poll dating back to 1936, five of the top seven teams lost on the same afternoon, sparking a much-needed rebound opportunity for the perceived elites in Week 8. While next weekend's matchups within the top 25 fail to offer a litany of "good on good" games like last, the unpredictability of the sport this season continues to carry significant weight. The only unbeatens remaining at midseason are BYU , James Madison , Miami , Texas Tech , UCLA and Utah after most of the unblemished went down on Saturday. Could more fall in Week 8 to unranked foes? Let's take a look at the schedule and early lines. Odds via FanDuel Sportsbook. The big games No. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas (-3.5 ): Will the Longhorns rebound as a home favorite against the Rebels, or will Steve Sarkisian lose a third straight SEC game and bring more questions to the Forty Acres this season? It benefits Texas if defensive end Colin Simmons , who leads the country with 10.5 sacks, returns after being carted off against Florida , but his injury status remains unknown. Trinidad Chambliss is the SEC's top individual playmaker at quarterback and has already had his way against two nationally-ranked opponents this fall with impressive wins over LSU and Missouri . No. 6 Indiana (-7.5) at Michigan : Backup quarterback Tommy Carr provided an immediate spark for the Wolverines against Penn State , leading multiple second-half touchdown drives after being plucked from the bench ahead of Bryce Underwood . Manufacturing that same level of success against the defending national champions, who saw their nation-leading 22-game winning streak snapped vs. Ohio State , is a different task entirely. Indiana hasn't won at Michigan Stadium since 1967, which is perhaps why this opening line seems a bit on the low side. No. 11 Tennessee (-2.5) at South Carolina : Can Shane Beamer knock off another top-15 SEC opponent with the Gamecocks? He's had an extra week to prepare -- 3-4 overall at South Carolina in that spot -- for what the Vols bring to Williams-Brice Stadium in a pivotal matchup for Tennessee's lasting CFP hopes. The Gamecocks clicked for the first time all season offensively last time out at Florida after LaNorris Sellers accounted for five total touchdowns. These two have split their last eight meetings dating back to 2016. No. 14 Houston at No. 10 Utah (-5.5) : The Utes survived a Big 12 warning shot at Colorado on Saturday night and now get a red-hot Cougars squad hoping to occupy one of the conference's multiple seats at the CFP table. Houston held off Oklahoma State , 35-32, in Week 7 behind Conner Weigman's five touchdown passes. For Utah, protecting home turf means preserving its unbeaten record and strengthening a playoff résumé that needs its first quality win with BYU looming on Nov. 7. No. 18 LSU (-6.5) at Auburn : Alex Golesh and the Tigers just knocked the SEC's king off the throne and now comes the tricky part: doing it again at home with everyone paying closer attention. LSU's coming off a 31-point demolition of Mississippi State and knows the margin for error is near zero the rest of the way in SEC play. Was Auburn's win between the hedges a turning point for the program or this season's signature moment? We'll know more after Week 8 inside Jordan-Hare. So, where does everyone stand in Week 8? Week 7 saw five of the top seven teams in the country – Georgia, Notre Dame, Indiana, Alabama and Texas – all lose, which shook up the odds to win the National Championship in the 2026 season. That’s also changed the latest AP Poll, as there are a bunch of two-loss teams in the SEC that are fighting for a top spot in the conference. The SEC and Big Ten are both becoming very interesting, as a bunch of national title contenders have a loss on their resume at this point in the season. In the Big 12, Texas Tech, BYU and Utah all continue to dominate to open the season, though the Utes have a tough matchup with Houston in Week 8. The top teams in the latest AP Poll (No. 1 Miami, No. 2 BYU and No. 3 Ohio State ) feature a team from the ACC, Big 12 and Big Ten. Fortunately for the Rebels, most of the players listed as out have been absent for several weeks, allowing the coaching staff time to adjust rotations and personnel packages. Ole Miss also continues to have just one player listed as questionable in tight end Hayden Bradley, while defensive backs Antonio Kite, MJ Preston and Ladarian Clardy remain listed as probable. If those three are able to play, it would help offset some of the losses in the secondary caused by Joseph and Nascar McCoy being unavailable. Missouri's report had six players listed as out, including running back Ahmad Hardy and safety JaDon Blair. Two more players are listed as doubtful, while linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr. and defensive tackle Sterling Webb remain questionable. Perhaps the most interesting names on Missouri's report are former Ole Miss players Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee . Both are listed as probable entering the weekend and appear to be trending toward availability for Saturday's game. It would not be surprising to see either player removed from the report on Friday or prior to kickoff as Missouri prepares for one of the SEC's featured matchups this weekend. Kentucky Football continues to climb in the AP Top 25 Poll , moving up three spots to No. 12 after defeating Oklahoma, 21-13, in Norman. The Wildcats improved to 6-1 overall, became bowl eligible, and strengthened their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff in head coach Will Stein’s first season. The victory was far from perfect, as Kentucky’s offense struggled to find consistency after an impressive opening drive. However, the defense came up with several crucial plays down the stretch to help the Wildcats secure another impressive road win. Kentucky’s offense looked sharp on its opening possession, slicing through Oklahoma’s defense and setting the tone early. However, the unit stalled after that drive and did not score another offensive touchdown until 12:53 remained in the fourth quarter, when quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Willie Rodriguez for the Wildcats’ second touchdown of the game. Although the final score was relatively low, Kentucky’s defense also struggled at times in the first half. Safety Jordan Castell came up with a key interception when Oklahoma attempted a fake field goal in the first quarter, ending a promising Sooners possession. The Wildcats’ defense began to turn things around late in the third quarter when Ty Bryant intercepted Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer, giving Kentucky possession in Sooners territory. From there, the defense took control. Oklahoma recorded two three-and-outs and threw two more interceptions. Castell returned one for a pick-six, extending Kentucky’s lead to eight points, while Bryant secured the game-ending interception to seal the victory. While the game was sloppy on both sides, Kentucky found a way to finish strong. The Wildcats improved to 6-1, earned bowl eligibility, and continued building momentum as they pursue a potential College Football Playoff appearance. Now, Kentucky returns home to Kroger Field to face Vanderbilt, looking to avenge consecutive losses to the Commodores while losing three of four in the series. Kentucky fell 45-17 on the road last season after suffering a 20-13 defeat at home the year before. With Vanderbilt struggling through a disappointing season, the Wildcats will have an opportunity to extend their winning ways and continue climbing the national rankings. But if this last weekend showed us anything, it’s that upsets are commonplace this season, and Kentucky can’t afford to come out flat against a Commodores team starving for its first SEC win of the season. That, and Vandy did nearly pull off an upset over an Auburn team that just won at No. 1 Georgia. The Dores may be struggling, but they’ve still got an SEC roster. Vanderbilt Commodores (3-4, 0-4 in SEC) Vanderbilt has struggled through the first seven games of the season, and life after former quarterback Diego Pavia has been challenging. The Commodores finished the 2025 regular season with an impressive 10-2 record before losing to Iowa in the Citrus Bowl, ending the year at 10-3. However, the Dores have not come close to replicating that success this season. Vanderbilt suffered a disappointing 31-21 loss to Arkansas this past weekend. The Razorbacks entered the matchup on a 14-game Southeastern Conference losing streak, but they snapped that drought against the Commodores. One of Vanderbilt’s biggest challenges has been the development of 5-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The young signal-caller has shown flashes of his talent, but his inexperience has been evident. The drop-off from Pavia to Curtis has been noticeable, and Vanderbilt’s decision to start a true freshman at quarterback has come with growing pains. Through seven games, Curtis has completed 101/161 passes for 62.7%, totaling six passing touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also been sacked 11 times. Curtis measures 6-foot-3 and weighs 230 pounds, giving him the physical tools to develop into a quality quarterback. He can also make plays with his legs, recording 55 carries for 144 rushing yards and two touchdowns. However, his turnover numbers and struggles under pressure will be areas Kentucky looks to exploit. Vanderbilt’s other major weakness has been its defense, particularly against the run. The Commodores have struggled to establish consistency along their front seven, which could create problems against Kentucky’s rushing attack. The Wildcats have a three-headed backfield featuring CJ Baxter, provided he is healthy enough to play, alongside Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes. If Kentucky can keep all three involved, Vanderbilt could have a difficult time slowing down the ground game. Kentucky’s offensive line, known as the Big Blue Wall, has also looked impressive this season. If the unit continues to open running lanes and control the line of scrimmage, the Wildcats could have a significant advantage. As for Vanderbilt’s offense, Curtis has several weapons at his disposal. Senior wide receiver Junior Sherrill has emerged as Curtis’ primary target. The 5-foot-11, 200-pound receiver has recorded 41 receptions for 628 yards and four touchdowns so far this season. Junior wide receiver Ja’Cory Thomas provides another option at 6-foot-3 and 215 pounds. He has recorded 12 receptions for 195 yards and one touchdown. Vanderbilt also features junior tight end Jayvontay Conner, who stands 6-foot-4 and weighs 235 pounds. Conner has totaled 13 receptions for 146 yards, though he has yet to score a touchdown this season. Junior receiver Tristen Brown has added another option in the passing game, recording 12 receptions for 145 yards. In the backfield, Vanderbilt relies primarily on two running backs. Senior Sedrick Alexander, who stands 5-foot-9 and weighs 207 pounds, has recorded 61 carries for 270 yards and five touchdowns. Senior Makhilyn Young, at 5-foot-10 and 210 pounds, has added 52 carries for 216 yards and two touchdowns. For Vanderbilt to pull off the upset, Curtis will need to protect the football, make better decisions under pressure, and find ways to move the ball against Kentucky’s defense. The Commodores will also need to improve against the run to keep the Wildcats’ offense from controlling the game. Kentucky, meanwhile, will look to establish the run early, protect Minchey, and continue creating turnovers defensively. With the Wildcats playing at home and Vanderbilt struggling in SEC play, Kentucky has an opportunity to deliver another convincing win against a team that’s had its number. How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Vanderbilt Commodores Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Time: 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 24 TV Info: SEC Network Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as an 11.5-point favorite. ESPN gives Kentucky an 85.4% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 6-1 and bowl eligible, with its attention now turning toward the College Football Playoff. Under first-year head coach Will Stein, the Wildcats have shown they can win in different ways, whether through explosive offensive performances or clutch defensive plays in lower-scoring games. Vanderbilt, meanwhile, is reeling after falling to 3-4 overall and 0-4 in SEC play. Losing to Arkansas after the Razorbacks had endured a 14-game conference losing streak raises further questions about the direction of the Commodores’ season. Kentucky also has extra motivation after losing to Vanderbilt in each of the past two seasons. home.headline: Mailbag: How will CJ Baxter, other injuries affect Kentucky's playoff outlook?
home.blurb: Baxter was listed as a game-time decision on the pre-Oklahoma availability report. He participated in warmups and was running sprints on the sideline throughout the game but didn’t actually play. Vanderbilt is winless in SEC play, but Kentucky must still be on alert this week. This team needs a bye week to rest a variety of injuries, but I would be wary about holding anyone out against the Commodores who can play at other positions with less depth. The linebacker depth should be helped by the return of Alex Afari, but he did not play in Oklahoma, even after a judge made him eligible on Friday. The injuries for backup linebacker Antwan Smith and backup nickel back Jaden Smith appear to be long-term issues, so do not expect them back soon. Wide receiver Nic Anderson’s status will be worth watching this week too after he appeared to reaggravate his arm/shoulder issue in Oklahoma. But for this Kentucky team, it wasn’t even the highlight of the month. Kentucky rode its opportunistic defense to a 21-13 win over Oklahoma to move to 6-1 on the season and 4-1 in SEC play. The No. 12 Wildcats are tied for first place in the SEC and seem likely to be slotted in a projected playoff spot when the committee releases its first ranking on Nov. 3, as long as Will Stein’s team takes care of business against Vanderbilt this week. Regardless of what happens from here, Stein has given Big Blue Nation reason to dream. home.headline: Oklahoma vs. Kentucky Injury Report: Sooners offensive line banged up
home.blurb: After initially being listed as questionable, Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta, a pair of players who have started a number of games for the Sooners over the last two seasons, were downgraded to doubtful. They joined fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis as doubtful. This comes after Head coach Brent Venables said Fasusi was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Well, it looks like we'll have to wait another week for Fasusi's return. With Fasusi, Ozaeta, and Pierre-Louis doubtful for Saturday, the Sooners will have another combination starting up front for the Sooners. Ryan Fodje will continue to start at left tackle with true freshman Noah Best at left guard. Jake Miakkula will be at center once again with E'Marion Harris at right tackle. That leaves right guard as the question mark. Peyton Joseph is probably the player coming off the bench to start for the Sooners. He's been a rotational player at guard this season, playing 47 snaps this season. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen has been ruled out for Saturday, putting Trystan Haynes in line to make his second straight start. For the Kentucky Wildcats , one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. He remains questionable for Saturday, and Pete Nakos of On3 says he'll be a game-time decision. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). Fasusi has missed the last four games after playing with a shoulder injury against UTEP. Ozaeta was banged up in warm-ups ahead of the Red River Showdown, but still played 59 snaps up front. The 6-foot-1, 228-pound senior did not practice this week and was observed with his arm in a sling before he was ruled out for Saturday’s game at Hawaii. Jason Eck said the preseason Mountain West Defensive Player of the Year’s bone break is in the same shoulder he hurt in the Rate Bowl on Dec. 27. Eck added that he does not believe Jaxton’s injury is season-ending, but expects him to miss an extended period of time. His designation was first released via an initial availability report from the Mountain West on Thursday, one that saw multiple key Lobos listed as out or questionable ahead of Saturday’s game. Late to seeing this: LB Jaxton Eck and CB Frankie Edwards III are OUT for Saturday’s game. WR Massiah Mingo and RB Kiefer Sibley are also questionable. https://t.co/5jqZVKeiZ5 Only one Lobo was newly ruled out for the rest of the season on the initial report: backup linebacker Nick Wheeler, who Eck said suffered a torn ACL. Without Jaxton and Wheeler, UNM is expected to rely on linebackers Mercury Swaim and Clay Martineau for the near future. Starting cornerback Frankie Edwards III (9 total tackles) has also been ruled out for Saturday’s game, per the league’s availability report. Eck said the 5-10, 178-pound junior suffered a concussion, and expects him to return as soon as next week. Wide receiver Massiah Mingo (ankle) and running back Kiefer Sibley (shoulder) are questionable for Saturday’s game, per the availability report. A 5-9, 170-pound freshman, Mingo has caught five passes for 56 yards; Sibley has rushed for 205 yards, the second-best mark on the team.
